name: MorrF

lead: MorrF (also written Morr-F or Morr F) is a combined topical solution of minoxidil and finasteride sold in India, labelled for androgenetic alopecia, or pattern hair loss. Pharmacy listings show 3% and 5% minoxidil versions.

The appeal is a thicker, fuller head of hair. Minoxidil is the established topical regrowth ingredient, and finasteride is the drug that reduces DHT, so topical combinations aim to put both on the scalp in one product.

paras: A product page describes applying the solution to a clean, dry scalp, avoiding eyes and broken skin, with results appearing over several months and early shedding noted as common. Hair-loss forum users discuss combined topicals as an alternative to oral finasteride.

A product page advises stopping if persistent redness, itching or scalp discomfort develops and says the product is formulated for men. Minoxidil's topical side effects include scalp irritation and unwanted hair growth elsewhere.[2] Retailer listings conflict on some details, so the label is the reference.

chain: Apply a minoxidil plus finasteride solution to the scalp
Minoxidil acts on follicles; finasteride targets DHT
angle.text: The product is marketed for pattern hair loss, so the goal is thicker hair and a fuller scalp. For minoxidil, Wikipedia reports benefits after 2 to 4 months, peaking around 12 months, and says it must be continued to maintain results.[2]

lead: MorrF is a brand of topical solution that combines minoxidil and finasteride, sold in India for androgenetic alopecia. Retailer listings show a 60 ml bottle in 3% and 5% minoxidil versions, and one product page names Thakore Pharmaceuticals Laboratories as manufacturer.[1]

Minoxidil is the best-known topical hair regrowth ingredient: Upjohn developed it in 1963, introduced it for blood pressure in 1971, and the FDA approved topical use for male baldness in 1988 under the name Rogaine.[2] Combinations of minoxidil with finasteride are of interest to people who want both actions on the scalp.
Wikipedia notes that a combination of finasteride, latanoprost and minoxidil (code name TH-07) was in phase 2 trials as of December 2023, so combined topicals remain an active research area.[2]

paras: Retailer pages list MorrF as a minoxidil and finasteride combination for the scalp. One product page describes it as supporting regrowth and slowing hair loss in pattern baldness and notes that early shedding before new growth is common.[1]
Listings disagree about strengths and who the product is meant for, so the label is the authority.

Topical minoxidil is used mainly for pattern hair loss, increasing hair counts and thickening follicles. Benefits appear after 2 to 4 months and peak around 12 months; regrowth is lost if use stops.[2] Common effects include itching, scalp irritation and unwanted hair elsewhere; alcohol and propylene glycol vehicles can dry the scalp.[2]
No studies found. Studies of minoxidil alone are summarised on its Wikipedia page, which also notes a related triple combination in phase 2 trials.[2]
Combined topical products are discussed in hair-loss communities as a way to use finasteride locally. A product page says women should consult a healthcare provider first.[1]
